extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, agency officials, contractors, and others involved in FOIA/reverse-FOIA disclosure disputes and agency records management
extracted.subtask_description: Legal and administrative standards for determining when agencies may disclose submitter-generated business or other potentially confidential information under FOIA and related statutes, and the procedural steps for submitters and agencies in contesting disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor identification of non-disclosable information and administrative appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors should identify any information which they believe is not subject to disclosure under 5 U.S.C. 552, and should specify the reasons why such information is not disclosable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Contract Compliance Officer will consider the contractor's claim and make a determination, within 10 days, as to whether the material in question is exempt from disclosure. The contract compliance officer will inform the contractor of such a determination. The contractor may appeal that ruling to the Director of OFCC within 10 days. The Director of OFCC shall make a final determination within 10 days of the filing of the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of information during compliance review as investigatory file (5 U.S.C. 552(b)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: During the conduct of a compliance review or while enforcement action against the contractor is in progress or contemplated within a reasonable time, all information obtained from a contractor under Subpart B except information disclosable under §§ 60-40.2 and 60-40.3 of this chapter is to be considered part of an investigatory file compiled for law enforcement purposes within the meaning of 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information obtained from a contractor under Subpart B shall be treated as exempt from mandatory disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act during the compliance review.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 C.F.R. § 70.21 — prohibition on Department employees disclosing certain information
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the provisions of 18 U.S.C. 1905, every officer and employee of the Department of Labor is prohibited from publishing, divulging, disclosing, or making known ... any information ... which information concerns or relates to the trade secrets, processes, operations, style of work, or apparatus, or to the identity, confidential statistical data, amount or source of any income, profits, losses, or expenditures of any person, firm, partnership, corporation, or association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No officer or employee of the Department of Labor shall disclose records in violation of this provision of law. No records of the Department of Labor with respect to matters specifically required by statute to be kept secret shall be made available for inspection or copying under the provisions of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 C.F.R. § 70.22 — discretionary disclosure of records in FOIA-exempt categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Department is not required by FOIA to make available materials or documents which are within categories described in 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(2), (4), (5), (6), (7), (8), or (9), under the Department’s disclosure policy particular records requested which come within these categories, or portions thereof, shall nevertheless be made available to the extent, but only to the extent, that the appropriate officer authorized to disclose information from Department records determines that the disclosure will further the public interest and will not impede the discharge of any of the functions of the Department of Labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a determination shall be made with due regard not only to the public interest in accessibility but also to the public interest in protecting citizens from impairment of their rights to privacy or from harassment, injury, or the dissemination of privileged or confidential information. Consider also whether disclosure would handicap, obstruct, or jeopardize effective performance of the Department’s functions, including law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 C.F.R. § 70.24(a) — exemption (4) for trade secrets and commercial/financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to exemption (4) ... the disclosure ... of matters that are trade secrets, and of commercial and financial information obtained from a person and privileged or confidential, may be refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure shall be refused where mandatory restrictions apply. Even where denial is not required, access cannot be granted under Department policy unless the disclosure officer determines that disclosure will serve the public interest and not impede the discharge of any function of the Department of Labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 C.F.R. § 70.24(b) — scope of exemption (4) to include customary privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent of the examination ... to protect privileged or confidential information is ... not restricted to the trade secrets and commercial or financial information specifically mentioned in the statute. Information the disclosure of which may be refused ... is intended to include information customarily subject to a doctor-patient, lawyer-client, or other such privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply exemption (4) to information typically protected by recognized privileges where confidentiality would customarily be expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 C.F.R. § 70.24(c) — meaning of 'obtained from any person' and cross-agency confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Information 'obtained from any person' would include information obtained from a person inside as well as outside the Government. While information which is confidential in the hands of one agency retains its protected character in the hands of agencies to which it was subsequently furnished, the exemption does not sanction the rendering of documents confidential by the expedient of transferring them among agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality status generally follows the information across agencies, but agencies cannot evade disclosure rules merely by transferring documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 C.F.R. § 70.24(d) — protection for items valuable as property (formulae, designs, research data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure in certain circumstances may be refused of material such as formulae, designs, drawings, research data, and the like, which are significant not as records but as items of valuable property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where similar property in private hands would be held in confidence, the public interest would appear to require that such property in the hands of an agency should be protected under exemption (4).

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 C.F.R. § 70.24(e) — confidentially furnished information
rubrics_metrics.description: This exemption is further intended to extend protection to other information in Government records which has been furnished and accepted in confidence and which would not customarily be released to the public by the person from whom the Government obtained it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exemption assures the confidentiality of information obtained through questionnaires and required reports to the extent that the information would not customarily be made public by the source. Agencies should give due consideration to such understandings and discourage unwarranted expectations of confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 C.F.R. § 70.24(f) — exemption (8) for financial institution examination reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to exemption (8) ... the disclosure from Department of Labor records of any matter contained in, or related to, examination, operating, or condition reports prepared by, on behalf of, or for the use of an agency responsible for the regulation or supervision of financial institutions, may be refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access will be refused where disclosure is not legally permitted or where a determination to disclose is inappropriate for reasons discussed in the other paragraphs. If another agency is concerned, § 70.31 procedures apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 C.F.R. § 70.31 — coordination and transfer when other agencies have primary interest
rubrics_metrics.description: If the release of a record in custody of the Department of Labor would be of concern not only to the Department but also to another Federal agency, the record will be made available by the Department only if its interest in the record is the primary interest and only after coordination with the other interested agency. If the interest of the Department in the record is not primary, the request will be transferred promptly to the agency having the primary interest, and the applicant will be so notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release of information received from another agency and the release to another agency of information collected from persons outside the Government shall be subject to the conditions and restrictions imposed by 44 U.S.C. 3508.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA exemptions are discretionary (permissive) not mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: The FOIA’s nine categories of exempt information disclose a Congressional concern that disclosure of certain information might injure interests in privacy or confidentiality, but the exemptions do not make non-disclosure mandatory nor do they provide an implied cause of action for submitters to prevent disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies have discretion to withhold exempt information, but FOIA does not, by its language or history, imply a private action for submitters to enjoin disclosure; the exemptions were intended as discretionary exceptions to the general duty of disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing test for disclosure determinations (public interest vs. confidentiality/agency functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether access to such records will be permitted, due consideration shall be given to the public interest in accessibility to information regarding operations of their Government but also to the public interest in protecting citizens from impairment of their rights to privacy or from harassment, injury, or dissemination of privileged or confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider whether disclosure would handicap, obstruct, or jeopardize effective performance of the Department's functions, including law enforcement; disclosure may be allowed only if it will further the public interest and not impede the Department's functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18 U.S.C. § 1905 — 'not authorized by law' limitation and agency regulation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1905 prohibits disclosure by government employees of certain categories of confidential business information but only as to disclosures 'not authorized by law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures pursuant to validly adopted agency regulations are 'authorized by law' and therefore not subject to the prohibitions of § 1905; agency authority to promulgate such regulations may rest on the housekeeping statute (5 U.S.C. § 301) or other specific enabling statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5 U.S.C. § 301 (housekeeping statute) as source of authority for disclosure regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of an executive department may prescribe regulations for the custody, use, and preservation of its records, papers, and property. This section does not authorize withholding information from the public or limiting the availability of records to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 301 has been treated as a separate source of agency authority for promulgation of disclosure regulations. Disclosures made pursuant to valid § 301-based regulations are 'authorized by law' and thereby immune from § 1905 prohibitions; legislative history of the 1958 amendment does not eliminate longstanding rulemaking authority under § 301.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency may release with deletions and proceed despite pending appeals where statutory time constraints apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to time constraints imposed by amendments to the Act, an agency may determine it cannot wait for the results of an administrative appeal and proceed to release subject documents with deletions after a short period (example: 5 working days after receipt of notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should document the exceptions and reasons; submitters may still have administrative appeal rights but those appeals may not indefinitely delay release.
